categories.main_business_segments: McKesson operates four reportable segments: U.S. Pharmaceutical (distributes branded, generic, specialty, and OTC drugs; provides practice management and technology solutions to oncology and specialty practices; offers solutions to pharmacies and healthcare providers), Prescription Technology Solutions (connects patients, pharmacies, providers, and biopharma companies to address medication access, affordability, and adherence challenges), Medical-Surgical Solutions (provides medical-surgical supply distribution and logistics to healthcare providers), and International (provides distribution and services in Europe and Canada, with operations primarily in Norway and Canada following European divestitures).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: McKesson leverages technology-enabled distribution systems including McKesson Connect (internet-based ordering system), pharmacy automation solutions like ExpressRx Track, Six Sigma methodology for operational efficiency, electronic health record system integrations, data analytics capabilities, and real-world evidence platforms through Ontada. The company operates a network of distribution centers utilizing advanced inventory management systems, automated replenishment technologies, and forecasting software to optimize pharmaceutical and medical-surgical product distribution.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include retail national account chains, community pharmacies, institutional healthcare providers (hospitals, health systems, long-term care), oncology and specialty practices, physician offices, surgery centers, nursing homes, home health agencies, pharmacy benefit managers, health plans, and biopharma companies. End markets served include primary care, extended care, government programs, and specialty therapeutic areas including oncology, rheumatology, and ophthalmology.
categories.geographic_coverage: McKesson operates primarily in North America with major presence in the United States and Canada. The company previously operated extensively in Europe but completed divestitures of Austrian, UK, and EU businesses in fiscal 2022-2023, retaining only operations in Norway. The U.S. Pharmaceutical segment operates through 29 distribution centers, while Medical-Surgical Solutions operates through a network of U.S. distribution centers.
categories.supply_chain_position: McKesson operates as a midstream distributor in the pharmaceutical and medical-surgical supply chain, positioned between manufacturers and end-users (pharmacies, hospitals, healthcare providers). The company also provides downstream services including specialty pharmacy, retail pharmacy operations, and direct patient services through its oncology and specialty practice networks.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include building an integrated oncology service business, expanding biopharma services, advancing medication access and affordability solutions, developing data analytics and real-world evidence capabilities, and enhancing technology platforms for healthcare ecosystem connectivity. R&D investments focus on prescription technology solutions, clinical decision-support tools, and digital health innovations. The company invested $89 million in R&D in fiscal 2023.
categories.revenue_model: McKesson generates revenue primarily through product distribution (pharmaceutical and medical-surgical supplies) with margins based on volume and pricing, supplemented by service revenues from technology solutions, practice management services, consulting, logistics, and specialty pharmacy services. The company also receives consideration from manufacturers based on purchase percentages and inflation-based components, and generates revenue from government contracts for vaccine distribution and ancillary supply kits.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors in pharmaceutical distribution include AmerisourceBergen Corporation and Cardinal Health, Inc. In medical-surgical distribution, McKesson competes with national and regional medical supply distributors. In RxTS, competitors include biopharma services companies, software firms, and consulting companies. McKesson's competitive advantages include scale, diversity of product and service offerings, extensive customer relationships, and integrated technology platforms. The company is one of the largest healthcare services leaders in North America.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: McKesson is a large-cap company with approximately $276.7 billion in revenues for fiscal 2023 (5% growth versus prior year), $12.4 billion in gross profit, and $3.6 billion in net income attributable to McKesson. The company has approximately 51,000 employees worldwide. Market capitalization was approximately $48.2 billion as of September 2022. The company demonstrates consistent growth in U.S. Pharmaceutical and RxTS segments, with strategic focus on higher-margin specialty and technology services.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: McKesson differentiates through comprehensive integrated solutions spanning the entire patient medication journey from access to adherence, advanced technology platforms connecting healthcare ecosystem participants, extensive distribution network with 29 U.S. pharmaceutical distribution centers and 285,000+ medical-surgical products, specialty expertise in oncology and complex therapies, data analytics and real-world evidence capabilities, and scale advantages enabling competitive pricing and service reliability. The company emphasizes making quality healthcare more accessible and affordable while supporting improved patient outcomes.
